description: A plain HTTP fetch of https://bqk-kos.org/?lang=en returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, while search engines index the same site richly and deep PDF URLs are widely referenced.

result.result_summary: Hypothesis: WAF/bot filtering on non-browser user agents, not a dead site. Treat as bot-defended-but-live and unverified; retry with a headless browser and realistic headers before recording any bqk-kos.org URL as unreachable.

why_it_matters: The entire cell depends on this one domain. If the collector is configured with a naive fetcher, every CBK source will falsely register as dead.

description: No searchable/queryable online licence register (database UI or API) was found for CBK-licensed institutions; the register appears to be published only as dated PDF snapshots (e.g. Lista-e-institucioneve-financiare-22.04.2026-ALB.pdf).

result.result_summary: Albanian searches for a 'regjistri i institucioneve të licencuara' returned only PDF lists and, for the equivalent live registry concept, Bank of Albania pages — not a Kosovo one. Collection must therefore be PDF-snapshot-and-diff based.

why_it_matters: Licence entries/exits and PSP/EMI authorisations can only be detected by differencing successive PDFs, which raises collection cost and latency versus an API-backed register.

description: Albanian-language queries about Kosovo payment/e-money institution registers are heavily contaminated by Bank of Albania (bankofalbania.org) results, because both regulators publish in Albanian using near-identical terminology ('institucionet e parasë elektronike', 'institucionet e pagesave').

result.result_summary: Several searches returned Albanian (AL) rather than Kosovar (XK) sources on the first page. Noisy terms flagged: 'institucionet e parasë elektronike', 'institucionet e pagesave', 'licencimi'.

why_it_matters: Automated query expansion in Albanian will silently pull in the wrong jurisdiction unless queries are domain-scoped (site:bqk-kos.org) or paired with 'Kosovë'/'BQK'.

description: No CBK page was found that republishes the individual audited annual financial statements of each licensed commercial bank; what the CBK publishes at institution level appears to be statistical reporting (assets, capital) via time series and monthly releases.

result.result_summary: Searches in Albanian for 'pasqyrat financiare individuale bankat komerciale' returned CBK's own statements and aggregate statistics, not per-bank IFRS statements.

why_it_matters: Per-bank audited statements likely have to be collected from the banks' own investor-relations/disclosure pages or from the business registry — a gap another A1 cell must cover.

description: Law 08/L-328 on Payment Services is referenced inside a 2025 CBK regulation, but no Official Gazette record for it was located in this pass; only a Government-hosted draft (PROJEKTLIGJI PER SHERBIMET E PAGESAVE, 2026) was found.

result.result_summary: gzk.rks-gov.net search did not surface 08/L-328. Status of the enacted text is unresolved — recorded as unverified, not absent.

why_it_matters: The payment-services regime is the single most consequential regulatory variable for payments market entry; ambiguity about which text is in force must be resolved before drawing conclusions.

description: Two non-canonical hosts serving CBK content were observed in search results: env2.bqk-kos.org and bqk.hpdevenv.com (both appear to be staging/development mirrors).

result.result_summary: These mirrors index in search engines and may serve stale or pre-release content.

why_it_matters: A collector could ingest staging content as authoritative. Canonicalise all CBK URLs to the bqk-kos.org host and blocklist the mirrors.

description: No bank-published shareholder general-assembly notices ('njoftim për kuvendin e aksionarëve', 'ftesë për mbledhjen e përgjithshme të aksionarëve') were located for any Kosovo commercial bank, in Albanian or Serbian.

result.result_summary: The Albanian-language query returned only the Law on Business Organizations (Ligji për Shoqëritë Tregtare) as published via ARBK/MINT and unrelated 2025 political items — no actual bank convocation notices.

why_it_matters: Kosovo's banks are unlisted, so there is no exchange-disclosure obligation forcing convocation notices onto a public feed. The shareholder-governance layer of workstream A1 therefore has to be reconstructed from the company registry (ARBK) and from annual-report governance chapters, not from an IR notices feed. Collection design should not assume this feed exists.

description: No Serbian-language ('sr') disclosure channel was found on ANY Kosovo commercial bank's own website. The sr-language search returned only Serbia-domiciled sister banks (procreditbank.rs, nlbkb.rs), NBS's Serbian bank-balance-sheet portal, and CBK's own ?lang=sr pages.

result.result_summary: Serbian-language hits for 'godišnji izveštaj / revidirani finansijski izveštaji' resolved to Serbia, Montenegro or the Kosovo regulator — not to Kosovo bank IR pages. Kosovo bank IR appears to be sq + en only.

why_it_matters: The sr-language requirement for this cell can only be met at the regulator layer, not the bank-own layer, and there is a real risk of mis-attributing Serbia-domiciled ProCredit/NLB filings to their Kosovo namesakes. Entity disambiguation rules (domain + legal entity name) are mandatory in the collector.

description: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo's disclosure documents are effectively absent from search indexes; only the container page /en/financial-statements/ was found, with a call-centre phone number and info@teb-kos.com as the stated route to more information.

result.result_summary: Two separate queries (bank-name and domain-scoped exact-phrase) returned no TEB annual report or audited statement PDF. A paywalled aggregator (The Banker Database) held TEB Kosovo data instead.

why_it_matters: TEB is a major Kosovo bank; if its own channel is JS-rendered or gated, a plain HTTP scraper will silently produce a coverage hole for one of the largest institutions. Requires a rendering fetcher and an explicit completeness check.

description: No financial reports or disclosure section were located for PriBank Sh.A. (pribank-ks.com) or İŞBANK Kosova (isbankkosova.com) via sq or en search.

result.result_summary: Queries returned other banks' reports plus the licensed-bank roster; nothing bank-own for either institution.

why_it_matters: These are the two smallest/newest licensed banks. Their absence from the own-disclosure layer means market-total reconstruction from bank-own sources alone will be incomplete and must be closed with CBK aggregate data.

description: The Kosovo Banking Association's own canonical domain could not be confirmed. The seed-implied bankassoc-kos.com did not appear in any search result.

result.result_summary: Only a member bank's descriptive page (bkt-ks.com) and an official Facebook page surfaced for 'Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës'.

why_it_matters: The association is the natural aggregation point for sector-level positions and member lists; without its canonical site, that layer depends on social media and second-hand pages. The domain must be resolved before it is trusted — it is recorded here as unconfirmed, not as dead.

description: Multiple host variants serve the same NLB Kosovo documents (nlb-kos.com, www.nlb-kos.com, hr.nlb-kos.com), and Banka Ekonomike serves its archive from two path families after an apparent CMS migration (/Articles/68/Images/... and /wp-content/uploads/...).

result.result_summary: Identical or near-identical PDFs are reachable under several hosts/paths; some legacy links surfaced only via third-party document mirrors (yumpu, vdocuments) rather than the bank domain.

why_it_matters: Without canonicalisation the corpus will double-count reports and produce false 'new disclosure' events; third-party mirrors must never be treated as primary because their fidelity is unverified.

description: No functioning, publicly disclosing Serbian-system bank operating inside Kosovo was found. Legacy entities surfaced in sr search (Jugobanka/Jugbanka Kosovska Mitrovica, Kosovska Banka) appear only in directory listings and encyclopaedic entries, not as live disclosure publishers.

result.result_summary: Directory aggregators (imenik.rs, planplus.rs) and Wikipedia returned entries; no corporate site with financial statements or press releases was located.

why_it_matters: Means the 'parallel banking system' side of the cell has no first-party issuer disclosure at all — everything must be reconstructed from NBS, Poštanska štedionica, government offices and local media, which raises the evidential burden on those sources.

description: No Serbian-language banking-industry association or aggregator specific to Kosovo was found. Searches for a Kosovo bankers' association in sr returned only CBK material.

result.result_summary: Queries returned bqk-kos.org pages exclusively; no association portal in sr surfaced.

why_it_matters: An industry association would normally be the cheapest pointer to member banks, fee schedules and sector statistics. Its absence in sr means the Albanian-language association (if any) must be covered by the sq cell and cross-linked.

description: Several sr query terms are structurally noisy and must be constrained. 'Mitrovica' collides heavily with Sremska Mitrovica (Serbia proper); 'Kosovska Banka' is largely a historical/encyclopaedic entity; 'platni promet' alone returns generic Serbian domestic-payments content.

result.result_summary: The query 'Kosovska Mitrovica sever bankarske usluge platne kartice dinar' returned at least one irrelevant Sremska Mitrovica bank-directory result.

why_it_matters: Untuned sr queries will pollute the collection pipeline with Serbia-proper banking content; queries must pin 'Kosovska Mitrovica'/'sever Kosova'/'KiM' and exclude 'Sremska'.

description: This cell is scoped to sr and regional/en coverage; no Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed here beyond incidental sq artefacts (EBRD PSD in Albanian, 'raportet vjetore').

result.result_summary: sq coverage intentionally deferred to the sq-scoped cells.

why_it_matters: Prevents double-counting but means the run must confirm that another cell actually covers sq issuer/regulator disclosure, or the primary-market view is incomplete.

description: Two candidate hosts were not fetched in this pass and their access status is a hypothesis, not a verdict: kim.gov.rs (Kancelarija za KiM) and posted.co.rs (observed only over http on a legacy path).

result.result_summary: Both were surfaced via search-result context rather than a direct successful fetch of the section pages.

why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass must resolve current canonical hosts before these are scheduled for collection; a legacy http path is a redirect/relocation risk, not evidence of a dead site.

description: Searched in Albanian for Assembly plenary and committee verbatim transcripts (transkript, procesverbal). Results pointed to a general archive area of kuvendikosoves.org covering older legislature periods (2001-2007, 2007-2019) but no current, dated, machine-addressable transcript index was located for the present legislature.

result.result_summary: Committee and plenary activity is currently observable mainly through news items and calendar entries rather than a structured transcript feed.

why_it_matters: Committee minutes are the cell's stated highest-value early-warning artefact; without a stable transcript endpoint, collection must fall back on news items, which are editorially summarised and drop speaker-level detail.

description: The Assembly appears under at least three hostnames (kuvendikosoves.org, assembly-kosova.org, assemblyofkosovo.org) and the finance ministry under two (mf.rks-gov.net, mfpt.rks-gov.net), with overlapping and possibly divergent content and path schemes.

result.result_summary: Same draft-law and committee IDs resolve under multiple hosts; canonical host not established in this pass.

why_it_matters: Risks duplicate records, broken monitors when one host is retired, and false 'dead source' verdicts during liveness checks.

description: No RSS/Atom or documented bulk/API endpoint for newly published acts was found on gzk.rks-gov.net; the portal exposes an ASP.NET search UI and per-act ActID pages only.

result.result_summary: New-act detection will likely need scheduled scraping of index pages or ActID range probing rather than a subscription feed.

why_it_matters: Determines the engineering cost and latency of the single most authoritative source in this cell.

description: GZK advertises Turkish and Bosnian act versions alongside sq/sr/en, but this run's language scope was sq/sr/en so no queries were run with Turkish or Bosnian banking/payments terminology.

result.result_summary: No candidates assessed in tr or bs.

why_it_matters: Minor for market intelligence, but relevant if entity-name matching needs all official transliterations.

description: Media reporting indicates the Constitutional Court annulled the Law on Payment Services adopted 5 December 2024, but the judgment itself was not retrieved from gjk-ks.org in this pass.

result.result_summary: Court judgment recorded as an unverified hypothesis; the gjk-ks.org candidate carries a reduced confidence score accordingly.

why_it_matters: The legal status of Kosovo's payment-services framework is the single most consequential fact in this cell and must not be recorded from media alone.

description: No Kosovo-specific KPMG landing page or KPMG Kosova sh.p.k. transparency report surfaced. Searches in English returned KPMG Serbia (Beograd) and KPMG International transparency reports instead.

result.result_summary: KPMG presence in Kosovo is attested only indirectly (US ITA country commercial guide lists KPMG among audit firms operating in Kosovo). The local legal entity, its registration status with KKRF, and whether it publishes a Kosovo transparency report all remain unverified.

why_it_matters: Big Four coverage of the Kosovo assurance layer is incomplete without KPMG; auditor-concentration analysis for Kosovo banks would be biased if a major signer is missing from the actor map.

description: Same gap for EY: no Kosovo-specific EY page, entity name, or transparency report was found in this pass.

result.result_summary: EY's Kosovo presence rests solely on a third-party listing (trade.gov commercial guide). No primary confirmation obtained.

why_it_matters: Either EY does not hold a Kosovo statutory audit licence (a meaningful market-structure fact) or its Kosovo footprint is simply poorly indexed — the two possibilities have opposite analytical implications and must be separated via the KKRF register.

description: The BQK's published register of approved external auditors of financial institutions is mandated by its own regulation ('Rregullore për Auditorët e Jashtëm') but the actual register page/URL was not located through search.

result.result_summary: Only the regulation PDFs were found; no direct URL to the live register of approved external auditors.

why_it_matters: This register is the highest-value single artefact for this cell — it authoritatively links audit firms to supervised banks. Its location must be resolved by browsing the BQK supervision section directly rather than via search engines.

description: The KKRF (Kosovo Council for Financial Reporting) own web portal was not confirmed. All KKRF instruments found were mirrored on third-party sites (SCAAK, IKAF, ATK, Gazeta Zyrtare).

result.result_summary: kkrf.rks-gov.net is a plausible but unverified address; a 2020 press report also alleged the body operated without inspectors, which may explain a thin or dormant web presence.

why_it_matters: Without the KKRF register, the audit-firm licensing picture must be reconstructed from the SCAAK directory and firm transparency reports, which are self-reported and incomplete.

description: Serbian-language (sr) coverage of the Kosovo audit/assurance layer is markedly thinner than Albanian. An sr query on Kosovo bank auditor reports returned mostly Serbian, Montenegrin and regional (NBS, CBCG) sources rather than Kosovo ones.

result.result_summary: The only substantive sr-language Kosovo hits were ZKA reports published as 'Kancelarija Generalnog Revizora' and BQK pages served via ?lang=sr. No Serbian-language Kosovo audit-firm publications were found.

why_it_matters: sr-language monitoring for this cell should be scoped to the official bilingual publishers (ZKA, BQK, Gazeta Zyrtare) rather than expecting an independent Serbian-language assurance-sector press; budgeting broad sr crawling here would waste effort.

description: No Kosovo-specific 'banking sector survey' or 'banking outlook' publication by a Big Four or mid-tier firm was found, despite it being an explicit seed hypothesis.

result.result_summary: Searches surfaced firm office pages and transparency reports, plus Deloitte Albania-and-Kosovo and Grant Thornton global banking content, but no dedicated Kosovo banking-sector survey.

why_it_matters: Advisory-firm sector surveys are usually a rich secondary intelligence stream. For Kosovo they appear not to exist as standalone products, so this cell must lean on transparency reports, signed audit opinions and the SAI channel instead.

description: No Kosovo-specific, bank-run fintech hackathon or innovation-challenge programme was found (searched sq and en). Regional analogues exist (Raiffeisen AI Hackathon BiH, Garaža FinTech AI Hackathon Belgrade, BoC Fintech Hackathon Cyprus, Regional AI Hackathon Albania which lists Kosovo participants) but no XK bank-branded edition surfaced.

result.result_summary: Only generic ICK hackathons and a 'Women and FinTech' incubator edition were identified for Kosovo; no bank-sponsored fintech hackathon confirmed.

why_it_matters: Absence itself is a signal: Kosovo banks appear to engage innovation ecosystems via sponsorship (KosICT) rather than by running their own challenges, so sponsorship pages — not hackathon sites — are the channel to monitor.

description: Serbian-language (sr) weak-signal channels for Kosovo banking/payments are very thin. Targeted sr queries for bank vacancies in Kosovska Mitrovica returned mostly Serbia-proper portals (Infostud, Jooble) and no Kosovo-bank career feed in Serbian.

result.result_summary: Only klikdoposla.com and bilingual portalpune.com produced any sr-language Kosovo hiring surface.

why_it_matters: North Kosovo banking/payments activity and Serbian-language institutional communication may be systematically under-observed in this cell.

description: Kosova Finance Forum was only reachable through media coverage (Telegrafi, Dukagjini); no official forum domain with agenda/sponsor PDFs was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Event confirmed (2nd edition, 27–28 April 2026, Pristina, 50+ speakers) but only via secondary reporting.

why_it_matters: Sponsor tiers and full agendas — the highest-value part of a conference as a weak signal — remain uncaptured until the primary site is found.

description: No Kosovo-domestic banking or fintech awards programme (national 'best bank'/'best digital bank' scheme run inside XK) was identified; recognition appears to come exclusively from international bodies (Euromoney, Global Banking & Finance Review).

result.result_summary: Searched 'çmimi banka më e mirë Kosovë' and English equivalents; only international award citations republished by banks were found.

why_it_matters: Award-based signal for XK must be harvested from international award pages plus bank advertorials, not from a local awards body.

description: No Kosovo Competition Authority decision specifically on bank commissions, interchange fees or account fees was identified. Albanian-language searches for 'Autoriteti i Konkurrencës vendim bankat komisionet' returned almost exclusively Albania's Autoriteti i Konkurrencës (caa.gov.al) cases against Albanian banks (e.g. Vendim 174, Raiffeisen/BKT investigations), not Kosovo's AKK.

result.result_summary: Kosovo AKK decisions register exists at ak.rks-gov.net/vendimet, but no banking/payments fee case surfaced in search results; publicised AKK cases in results concerned other sectors (e.g. fuel/NAFTA).

why_it_matters: The interchange/fee enforcement channel appears dormant or unindexed in Kosovo, so competition-authority output cannot yet be assumed as a fee-intelligence stream; the register must be enumerated directly rather than searched.

description: Albanian-language queries about Kosovo consumer/competition/ombudsperson topics are dominated by Republic of Albania institutions with near-identical names (Autoriteti i Konkurrencës, Avokati i Popullit) and domains (.gov.al, avokatipopullit.gov.al).

result.result_summary: Multiple searches returned Albanian rather than Kosovar institutions on the first page.

why_it_matters: Automated collection must domain-pin to .rks-gov.net / oik-rks.org / bqk-kos.org, or the corpus will silently fill with Albania data and corrupt Kosovo conclusions.

description: No centralised, official comparison table of bank fees/tariffs across all Kosovo banks was found (no BQK equivalent of, e.g., CBCG's 'Tarife banaka' comparison page in Montenegro, which did surface in the sr search).

result.result_summary: Fee disclosure in Kosovo is decentralised to each bank's own çmimorja PDF/page; the regional comparator that exists in Montenegro has no Kosovo counterpart in results.

why_it_matters: Cross-bank fee benchmarking requires assembling per-bank PDFs and normalising them; there is no single authoritative feed to track.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching returned useful CBK material (Godišnji izveštaj, finansijsko obrazovanje, žalbe terminology) but no Serbian-language Kosovo consumer-protection NGO, complaint portal, or bank tariff publication aimed at the Serb-majority market.

result.result_summary: sr-language coverage of this cell is essentially limited to CBK's own translated publications.

why_it_matters: Conduct and pricing intelligence for Serb-majority municipalities (and parallel-banking realities) is likely invisible in the sq/en corpus.

description: No dedicated financial ombudsman / alternative dispute resolution (ADR) body for banking disputes was identified for Kosovo; complaint escalation appears to end at BQK's consumer complaints division, with the general Ombudsperson covering public authorities and courts handling the rest.

result.result_summary: Searches for an ombudsperson-banking link returned the general Avokati i Popullit institution only.

why_it_matters: Absence of a financial ADR body means dispute-outcome data (rulings against named banks) is largely unavailable — BQK aggregates are the ceiling of available granularity.

description: Searching in Albanian for 'Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës' (Kosovo Banking Association, SHBK/KBA) returned no association website or association-published statistics in the result set; results redirected entirely to BQK/CBK pages.

result.result_summary: No confirmed URL for a Kosovo banking association aggregator this run. The actor is widely referenced in the sector, so absence is a search-coverage failure, not proof of non-existence.

why_it_matters: A national banking association is the classic private-sector aggregator of member-bank data and press releases and would be a high-value node in this cell.

description: No evidence found that S&P Global Ratings or Moody's assigns a sovereign rating to Kosovo; Fitch's April assignment was reported as Kosovo's first-ever sovereign rating and the country was previously the only Western Balkans state without one.

result.result_summary: Rating-agency coverage of Kosovo appears effectively single-source (Fitch), with Scope Ratings unverified.

why_it_matters: Single-agency coverage means no cross-agency triangulation on sovereign or bank credit views; the aggregator layer must lean harder on IMF/EBRD/EC analysis.

description: No full Kosovo FSAP was located. Kosovo had a 2012 FSAP and a 2020 IMF stocktaking of its recommendations, plus a Financial Sector Stability Review; Kosovo does not appear among mandatory-FSAP jurisdictions.

result.result_summary: FSAP material for Kosovo is sparse and dated; the FSSR is the practical substitute.

why_it_matters: Analysts expecting an FSAP-grade assessment must substitute the FSSR plus Article IV annexes, and should not assume FSAP-standard coverage of payment-system oversight.

description: ASK (Kosovo Agency of Statistics) does not produce monetary/financial or banking statistics; those responsibilities sit legally with BQK/CBK, with commercial banks and other financial corporations as reporting units.

result.result_summary: Targeting ASK for banking data is a dead end by design; ASK supplies macro denominators only.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort and mis-attribution of banking series to the statistical agency.

description: No Serbian- or Albanian-language term was found this run for the web-archiving concept as applied to Kosovo bank disclosures; Serbian and Albanian queries surfaced no local-language archiving initiative or national web archive for the .rks-gov.net / Kosovo domain space.

result.result_summary: The archive layer for Kosovo appears entirely foreign-operated (Internet Archive, archive.today).

why_it_matters: There is no domestic legal-deposit web archive to fall back on; if the Internet Archive misses a capture, the document is likely irrecoverable — argues for proactive Save Page Now on every disclosure URL.

description: Fitch Ratings and IMF eLibrary were not fetched directly this run; registration walls and PDF throttling are assumed from general behaviour, not observed.

result.result_summary: Access status for both is a hypothesis pending the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Do not classify either as blocked or dead on a single failed fetch during verification.

description: Searches for a standalone 'Kosovo segment' in RBI group reporting returned only the aggregated 'Southeastern Europe' segment (Albania, BiH, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kosovo, Romania, Serbia). Kosovo-level figures appear, if at all, in country tables/appendices rather than as an IFRS 8 reportable segment.

result.result_summary: SEE segment ~19% of group income in the Q1/2026 presentation per search snippet; no evidence found of a Kosovo-only reportable segment.

why_it_matters: Collection design must target country tables and appendix pages inside PDFs, not segment note headings; expect derivation rather than direct extraction.

description: Turkish-language searches for TEB A.Ş. investor material naming 'TEB Sh.A. Kosova' as an iştirak/bağlı ortaklık returned only general TEB annual reports and the BNP Paribas/Çolakoğlu ownership structure; no Kosovo-specific parent disclosure surfaced in this pass.

result.result_summary: Kosovo detail for TEB appears to live mainly at the local entity (teb-kos.com annual reports), not in the Turkish parent's IR pages.

why_it_matters: For the TEB chain the local subsidiary report is likely the primary source; KAP notification search should still be probed directly before concluding the parent publishes nothing.

description: Serbian-language querying produced useful results only for the NLB/Ljubljana disclosure chain; no Serbian-language parent-group disclosure route was found for the Kosovo units of Raiffeisen, ProCredit, TEB, BKT or Ziraat.

result.result_summary: Serbian terms used: 'rezultati', 'izveštaj', 'objave', 'Ljubljanska berza', 'banka'. Only NLB/LJSE material returned.

why_it_matters: Serbian is probably not a productive collection language for parent-group disclosures in this cell; effort should be reallocated to sq, en, de, tr and sl.

description: No Albanian-language reporting/disclosure vocabulary was found attached to Ziraat's Kosovo presence — it appears to operate as branches under a country directorate rather than a separately reporting legal entity.

result.result_summary: Ziraat annual reports list a Kosovo Country Directorate and branches in Prishtina, Prizren, Peja, Ferizaj; no Albanian-language 'pasqyrat financiare' page located for the Kosovo operation.

why_it_matters: Ziraat Kosovo data may only be obtainable from the Turkish parent report or the Kosovo regulator, not from a local-language corporate disclosure.

description: https://www.ziraat-kosova.com/ was referenced inside Ziraat annual-report content but was not independently fetched in this pass; its liveness and whether it hosts reports are unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: URL recorded as a candidate with access_status 'unverified'.

why_it_matters: Must be checked by the deterministic verification pass before being treated as a collection target.

description: No Visa or Mastercard press release, licensing notice or country page specific to Kosovo was located. Searches surfaced only generic Visa Ready / acquirer-licensing material with no Kosovo content.

result.result_summary: Scheme-operator primary communications for Kosovo appear absent from open search; scheme presence is visible only indirectly (Quipu contactless issuance, bank card portfolios).

why_it_matters: Scheme mandates and interchange notices are a core rail-change signal for this cell; without a scheme-side source, the cell depends entirely on BQK statistics and processor/bank announcements.

description: WebFetch of https://bqk-kos.org/sistemet-e-pagesave/?lang=en returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: Treated as bot-defended-but-live, not dead; other bqk-kos.org URLs appear in search indexes and PDFs resolve from the same host in search snippets.

why_it_matters: The most important source in this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher; a naive crawler will record the central bank as unreachable.

description: No dedicated national card-scheme or domestic switch operator (an analogue of Serbia's DinaCard or a national ATM/POS switch company) was found for Kosovo.

result.result_summary: Evidence points to card processing being outsourced to third-party processors (notably Quipu) and clearing being centralised in BQK's KIPS, with no separate scheme entity to track.

why_it_matters: Changes the actor map: for Kosovo, 'scheme operator' coverage collapses into BQK plus international schemes plus outsourced processors.

description: A Serbian-language BQK mirror for payment-system pages was not confirmed; the sr-language evidence found came from NBS and Serbian-language regional outlets rather than from BQK itself.

result.result_summary: BQK exposes ?lang= switching, but no sr payment-system page was retrieved this run.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of the Kosovo rail is currently sourced from the counterparty central bank, which carries a political frame.

description: No BQK tender or procurement notice for an instant-payment system or switch was found; the Albanian-language procurement query returned mostly Albania (app.gov.al) results due to sq-language ambiguity between Kosovo and Albania.

result.result_summary: e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net was identified as the correct portal, but no specific payments-infrastructure award was retrieved.

why_it_matters: Vendor identification for Kosovo's rail modernisation remains an open gap; the portal needs direct interactive search rather than web search.

description: All direct fetches to bqk-kos.org (HTML register page and the dated PDF list of licensed financial institutions) returned HTTP 403 during this run.

result.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on https://bqk-kos.org/mbikeqyrja-financiare/institucionet-financiare-te-licencuara-2/?lang=en and on the 22.04.2026 PDF. Search engines index the same URLs, so the site is bot-defended rather than dead. The exact list of licensed IP/IPE entities could NOT be read in this run and must be treated as unverified.

why_it_matters: The canonical actor list for this entire cell is behind that defence; without a headless-browser collector the pipeline cannot enumerate licensed EMIs/PIs authoritatively and will over-rely on media reports.

description: No Kosovo fintech/EMI/PI in this cell was found to operate a conventional investor-relations page, annual report, or structured press-release archive.

result.result_summary: Searches for funding/press releases returned coverage in third-party media (Telegrafi, Koha advertorials, SeeNews, The Recursive) and LinkedIn company pages, never a company newsroom or IR section. FIKS, the sector cluster, also has no news section.

why_it_matters: Workstream A1 topics (annual reports, investor relations, earnings) are structurally absent for non-bank payment actors in Kosovo; collection design must substitute media, advertorial and app-store channels or the cell will look empty.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching produced almost no Kosovo-specific non-bank payment sources.

result.result_summary: Queries in Cyrillic and Latin Serbian on doznake / platne institucije / transfer novca / Kosovska Mitrovica returned Serbia-domestic material (NBS payment-fee registers, Pošta Srbije PostCash, NLB Komercijalna) and the note that NLB Komercijalna closed its Kosovo branches in Feb 2024. No Kosovo-licensed Serbian-language payment institution or MTO source was identified.

why_it_matters: The Serb-majority north is a real remittance and cash corridor, but its payment infrastructure appears not to be documented in publicly indexed sr sources tied to Kosovo — a genuine blind spot rather than a search failure, and one that also implies parallel/unlicensed channels are invisible to this method.

description: Speculative Kosovo payment-gateway brand names (PCPS, Kosova Pay, Pay24, Klix) returned no evidence of existence in this market.

result.result_summary: The sq gateway query returned only regulatory PDFs, the eKosova state platform, and merchant blogs naming Paysera and Revolut as the practical acceptance options. None of the guessed brands were corroborated; they are recorded as not-found, not as sources.

why_it_matters: Confirms that domestic online-acquiring brands are thin or absent and that foreign EMIs (Paysera, Revolut) fill the gap — a structural fact about the cell, and a warning against seeding actor maps from guessed names.

description: "Kosovo e-Wallet" is not a payment product.

result.result_summary: The App Store app named Kosovo e-Wallet is a digital identity wallet published by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, not an e-money or payment wallet. Keyword-based collection on 'wallet' will produce false positives for this cell.

why_it_matters: Prevents mis-classification of a government identity credential as an EMI product in the actor map; also flags 'portofol digjital' as a noisy term.

description: No individual, currently published Kosovo contract award notice specifically for commercial banking services, payroll cards, POS acceptance or a treasury/payment software system could be surfaced through general web search in this pass.

result.result_summary: Searches in sq, sr and en returned the platform, the regulator, the legal framework and unrelated award PDFs (life insurance at BQK, a customs B08 form, a Tax Administration sr-language notice) but no banking/payment-specific award document. Such notices are almost certainly present but only retrievable inside the e-Prokurimi search interface or the OCDS dataset, which general search engines do not index.

why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be worked from search engines; the collection design must go through the OCDS API / portal query interface with CPV and keyword filters, not through crawling public search results.

description: The exact OCDS API base URL / bulk-download endpoint on the rks-gov.net platform was not established in this pass.

result.result_summary: Multiple secondary sources (Open Contracting Partnership, OCP Data Registry, Demokraci Plus Red Flags) independently state that KRPP publishes OCDS via an API on rks-gov.net and that data is downloadable in JSON/Excel/CSV, but no source in this pass exposed the literal endpoint string. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a dead end.

why_it_matters: The API is the single highest-value collection route for this cell; the exact endpoint must be resolved (via the OCP Data Registry publication page or by inspecting prokurimihapur.org / redflags.dplus.org network calls) before pipeline design.

description: No authoritative Albanian- or Serbian-language CPV label list for financial and banking services (CPV 66xxxxxx) was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: The Kosovo procurement rules confirm CPV is used and that large-value notices must be published in sq/sr/en, but the localised CPV vocabulary that would let a collector match category labels exactly was not retrieved.

why_it_matters: Without the localised CPV label set, keyword matching on sq/sr notice titles will be lossy and may miss awards phrased in non-obvious ways (e.g. 'sherbime financiare', 'mirembajtje e sistemit te pagesave').

description: Commercial aggregators covering Kosovo tenders (DevelopmentAid, BidsFactory) are subscription- or registration-gated.

result.result_summary: Listing pages are visible in search results but full tender and award text is behind a paywall; treated as blocked rather than absent.

why_it_matters: These cannot serve as a primary feed; the design must rely on the official portal and OCDS data, using aggregators only for alerting or translation.

description: Whether Kosovo municipalities and POEs procure banking services competitively at all, or hold them under legacy/non-tendered arrangements, could not be determined.

result.result_summary: No evidence either way surfaced in this pass. National Audit Office reports were identified as the place where such non-competitive or legacy banking arrangements would be criticised, but the specific finding was not located.

why_it_matters: If most public-sector banking relationships are untendered legacy arrangements, procurement notices will systematically under-represent the real market and audit reports become the primary evidence channel instead.

description: No dedicated donor/IFI portal was found that indexes Kosovo financial-sector projects in Albanian or Serbian. EBRD, EIB, World Bank projects/documents and TED are English-only for Kosovo financial-institution records; only scattered items (IFC /sq pressroom, World Bank /sq blog, WeBalkans language variants) exist locally.

result.result_summary: Local-language donor disclosure is press-release-level only; the underlying project and procurement records are English.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring cannot substitute for English IFI feeds in this cell; the sq/sr layer is useful for terminology and domestic amplification, not for primary project data.

description: Serbian/Cyrillic queries combining Kosovo with EBRD credit lines and the financial sector returned mostly North Macedonia, Serbia, Bosnia and Montenegro results, plus one Kosovapress sr-language item on Raiffeisen. Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo donor finance appears thin and is largely produced by Serbian-language Kosovo outlets rather than by donors.

result.result_summary: Sr-language search yields regional noise; no Kosovo-specific donor disclosure source in Serbian identified.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: sr coverage for this cell should be sourced from Kosovo Serbian-language media and the sr variants of Kosovo government portals, not from donors.

description: USAID appears repeatedly in the historical record for Kosovo financial-sector work (KCGF founding capital, Development Credit Authority guarantees, Investment Promotion and Access to Finance activity), but the most accessible USAID Kosovo material sits on an archived 2017-2020 subdomain, and the agency's status has changed materially since 2025.

result.result_summary: USAID sources are best treated as a historical baseline, not an ongoing feed.

why_it_matters: Building a live collector against USAID Kosovo pages would produce a dead or frozen feed; the ongoing US channel to track is MCC/MCA-Kosovo and any successor State Department assistance reporting.

description: The MCC Kosovo Compact (USD 202m, signed 2022) was checked for a digital-economy or payments component; published descriptions cover only energy storage and the JETA workforce project.

result.result_summary: MCC Kosovo is energy/workforce, not payments.

why_it_matters: Prevents over-weighting a large headline number that is irrelevant to banking and payments intelligence.

description: The KfW Entwicklungsbank Kosovo country-page URL recorded in this slice was inferred from KfW's standard country-page path pattern rather than returned by a search result; only a 2006 KfW Kosovo case study PDF (on findevgateway.org) was directly surfaced.

result.result_summary: KfW Kosovo project-database entry point is a hypothesis pending liveness verification.

why_it_matters: KfW is a top-three bilateral funder of Kosovo bank lending; the deterministic verification pass should resolve the correct current entry point rather than dropping the source.

description: No Mastercard or Visa press release naming a specific Kosovo bank partnership, contactless launch or tokenization deployment was located in this pass. Scheme newsrooms surfaced only global/EU-level announcements.

result.result_summary: Searched scheme newsrooms and general web; all hits were global tokenization/wallet stories with no Kosovo-specific item.

why_it_matters: Card schemes are usually a reliable indirect discloser of issuer-side product launches; their absence for Kosovo means issuer/processor changes must be inferred from app metadata, BQK card statistics and local media instead.

description: No public evidence found linking a Kosovo bank to a named card-management / issuer-processing platform (BPC SmartVista, OpenWay Way4, Nexi/SIA, Euronet) or to a named ATM hardware supplier (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos) for its Kosovo estate.

result.result_summary: Vendor-name searches returned only generic ATM-industry comparison articles; no Kosovo customer reference pages surfaced.

why_it_matters: Card issuing/processing and ATM hardware are core procurement categories for this workstream; the gap means supplier identity here currently rests on hypotheses that need a different route (procurement records, ATM screen/branding observation, job ads, EMV certification lists).

description: No Serbian-language (sr) vendor or bank disclosure specific to Kosovo banking technology procurement was found. The sr-language pass returned only the Central Bank of Kosovo's own Serbian-language site pages (payment-system oversight, laws, retail payments strategy) — regulatory, not vendor, content.

result.result_summary: Serbian query on core banking implementation/contract/supplier returned bqk-kos.org ?lang=sr pages and Wikipedia only.

why_it_matters: Serbian is a mandatory coverage language for Kosovo; the absence of sr vendor disclosure suggests supplier communication in this market runs in Albanian and English, and that sr coverage should be pursued via Serbian regional vendor/media outlets rather than Kosovo-hosted sr content.

description: No cybersecurity vendor was found publishing a named Kosovo bank as a customer reference. Kosovo-based security firms (Cyber Threat Defense, Cingerr, an unnamed Kosovo/Belgium boutique advertising via the Enterprise Europe Network) describe services but not banking clients.

result.result_summary: Searches returned service-listing and directory pages; no bank logos, no case studies, no partnership announcements.

why_it_matters: Bank security suppliers are normally kept confidential by design, so this category will likely never yield vendor-side disclosure; collection should pivot to BQK/regulatory IT-risk reporting, job advertisements and conference sponsorships.

description: A Printec Kosovo country contact page appeared in search results at a legacy-style URL (printecgroup.com/en/contact/27-contacts/6-kosovo.html) alongside the current site structure at printecgroup.com/offices-locations/. Not fetched, so its liveness is unknown and it may be a moved/legacy path.

result.result_summary: Two competing URL patterns for the same vendor's Kosovo presence; recorded as unverified rather than dead or live.

why_it_matters: Confirms a Kosovo office exists for at least one ATM/POS supplier, but the canonical Kosovo page must be resolved by the deterministic verification pass before being used as a monitored endpoint.

description: Searching in Serbian for a Kosovo-based Serbian-language business chamber or member registry (e.g. a Serb business association in North Mitrovica) returned only Serbia-proper institutions — Privredna komora Srbije, APR, and the Serbian Register of Chambers — plus a KoSSev news item about the Kosovo Chamber joining the ICC.

result.result_summary: No Kosovo-specific Serbian-language association or membership registry identified in this pass; Serbian-language coverage of my cell is currently empty.

why_it_matters: The Serb-majority north has its own business and banking arrangements; leaving it unmapped means the actor universe is incomplete and any 'complete list of institutions' claim would be wrong.

description: Queries in Albanian and English for a Kosovo fintech or payment-institutions association returned no such body. STIKK (ICT) and ICK (incubator) are the closest proxies; SHBK covers banks only.

result.result_summary: No 'Shoqata e Fintech-ut' or payment-institution association appears to exist for Kosovo.

why_it_matters: Non-bank payment institutions and e-money issuers have no membership pointer of their own, so they must be enumerated from the central bank's licence register and ARBK activity codes instead.

description: The Insurance Association of Kosovo (Shoqata e Sigurimeve të Kosovës) is well attested — founded 2002, 14 members — but no first-party website was located; only D&B, news and Facebook profiles surfaced. The speculative domain ask-ks.org was not confirmed and is NOT asserted as real.

result.result_summary: Association exists; canonical URL unknown after two sq queries.

why_it_matters: Without the first-party site there is no authoritative member list or publication feed for the insurance sector; the roster has to be reconstructed from BKS and the central bank register.

description: AmCham Kosovo, OEGJK/KDWV and AKB all publicise member counts (100+ activities, ~200 companies, 9,500+ members across 28 associations) but no machine-readable member directory was found in search results for any of them.

result.result_summary: Counts are public; lists are not, at least not via search.

why_it_matters: Member counts cannot substitute for named entities; these chambers may require direct requests, event-page mining, or logo-wall extraction to yield actual actor names.

description: Automated fetches of bankassoc-kos.com and amik.org both returned HTTP 403. Both domains are indexed by search engines and had content summarised in results, so these are treated as bot-defended-but-live, not dead.

result.result_summary: Two of the highest-value pointers in this cell need browser-grade collection.

why_it_matters: A naive HTTP collector would silently drop the two most important association registries in the cell and produce a false negative on the bank and microfinance actor lists.

description: No Albanian-language Kosovo outlet was found that operates a structured, machine-readable corporate press-release wire (a 'njoftim për media' distribution service) for banks. Bank releases appear to reach the public only via each bank's own site and via general news portals/agencies.

result.result_summary: Searches on 'njoftim për media bankë Kosovë' returned bank sites, BQK PDFs and general portals, but no PR-wire service.

why_it_matters: Release capture must be done outlet-by-outlet and bank-by-bank; there is no single sq wire to subscribe to, which raises collection cost and latency risk for A1.

description: Probes for the economy sections of gazetaexpress.com, kosova-sot.info and indeksonline.net did not return their section URLs; only homepages or encyclopedic entries surfaced.

result.result_summary: Site-path queries returned homepages / third-party pages rather than the requested /ekonomi sections.

why_it_matters: Section-level entry points for these outlets remain unconfirmed; a crawler needs the real section paths, so a targeted on-site navigation pass is required before these are added as feeds.

description: This cell is scoped to Albanian-language media, so Serbian-language (sr) Kosovo outlets (e.g. north-Kosovo Serb media) were not searched; sr terms such as 'bankarski sektor Kosovo', 'dobit banaka' were not used here.

result.result_summary: No sr-language queries were run in this slice by design.

why_it_matters: The sr signal layer for Kosovo banking/payments — especially the dinar/euro payments question and banking access in Serb-majority municipalities — is not covered by this slice and must be covered by a sibling cell.

description: RSS/Atom availability was not confirmed for any of the sq outlets listed; feed paths were inferred (e.g. WordPress /feed) but not tested.

result.result_summary: No feed URL was observed in search results.

why_it_matters: Collection method for most candidates is currently 'index crawl', which is more fragile and heavier than feed polling; a feed-discovery pass would materially cut cost.
